facts.statement: The genus Bernissartia was described by Dollo in 1883.
Bernissartia was a neosuchian crocodyliform that lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 130 million years ago.
facts.quote: Bernissartia ('of Bernissart') is an extinct genus of neosuchian crocodyliform that lived in the Early Cretaceous, around 130 million years ago.

facts.statement: Bernissartia reached a length of only 60 cm, making it one of the smallest crocodyliforms in history.
facts.quote: At only 60 cm in length, Bernissartia is one of the smallest crocodyliforms that ever lived.

facts.statement: Bernissartia possessed long, pointed front teeth for catching fish and broad, flat back teeth for crushing hard foods like shellfish and bones.
facts.quote: It had long, pointed teeth at the front of the jaws that would have been of use in catching fish, but broad and flat teeth at the back of its jaws that were suited for crushing hard food, such as shellfish, and possibly bones.

facts.statement: Bernissartia was probably semi-aquatic and resembled modern crocodilians in many respects.
facts.quote: It resembled modern species in many respects, and was probably semi-aquatic.

facts.statement: The primary fossil evidence for Bernissartia comes from skulls and skeletons found in the Sainte-Barbe Clays Formation of Belgium and the Camarillas Formation of Spain.
facts.quote: It is known primarily from skulls and skeletons found in the Sainte-Barbe Clays Formation of Belgium and the Camarillas Formation of Spain.

facts.statement: The genus Bernissartia is named after the Belgian locality of Bernissart where its remains were discovered.
facts.quote: Bernissartia (dedicado a Bernissart, localidad belga donde se encontraron sus restos) es un género extinto de crocodiliforme neosúquido de la familia Bernissartidae que vivió en el Cretácico Inferior.

facts.statement: Bernissartia belongs to the family Bernissartiidae.
Fossils of Bernissartia date from the Kimmeridgian to the Cenomanian stages, between 152.21 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Cenomanian (152.21 to 93.9 million years ago)
